## Personality

Jane is a plain, practical, and conscientious individual known for her steady, sensible, and lady-like demeanor. While recognized as nice and dutiful, she can also be strict and is noted for being crosser than [Anne](../character/anne.md), particularly when dealing with pupils who make funny speeches. Initially, her goal was to devote her entire life to teaching, remain unmarried, earn her salary fairly, please the school trustees, and earn a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor. However, she eventually marries, though her exceptional cooking skills present a unique challenge when her husband refuses to let her cook.

## History

[Jane Andrews](../character/jane-andrews.md) grew up in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) as a friend and schoolmate of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md). During their school years, she joined Anne's newly formed story club and entered the preparation class for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy). After passing the entrance examination alongside her classmates, she attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) and later took up a position teaching at the local [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school. Jane formed a close bond with [Anne](../character/anne.md) and her peers, participating in a spring birthday outing through the woods and joining a committee for the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society) that successfully convinced [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) not to place advertisements on his fence. Later, Jane resigned from teaching in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) with plans to move West in the fall. Before her planned departure, Jane hosted [Anne](../character/anne.md) for an overnight stay and proposed to her on behalf of her shy brother, [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md). Though [Anne](../character/anne.md) turned down the offer, Jane accepted the refusal composedly, remarking that [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md) would likely marry someone else instead.

## Quotes

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful."
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> "Even Levi Boulter or Lorenzo White would never stoop to that, tightfisted as they are. They would have too much respect for public opinion."
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P57](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0057)

> "I can’t understand how she could have wanted to live back here, away from everything,"
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P55](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0055)
